generic: Vi Capsular Polysaccharide of Salmonella Typhi (Typhoid Vi Polysaccharide Vaccine)
pharm: A purified Vi capsular polysaccharide antigen from Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi that induces protective anti-Vi (T-cell-independent) antibodies to prevent typhoid fever.
quick: Single 0.5 mL (25 mcg) intramuscular dose; revaccinate every 2-3 years if continued risk
Use only if clearly needed (inactivated antigen; risk to fetus not expected)
Considered compatible; benefit usually outweighs risk
Immediate hypersensitivity after injection; local/systemic reactions
summary: The Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine is an inactivated, single-dose typhoid vaccine made of the purified Vi (virulence) capsular polysaccharide of Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi. Given as one intramuscular injection, it stimulates anti-Vi antibodies that provide partial protection (roughly 55-70%) against typhoid fever for about 2-3 years, after which booster doses are needed for those at continued risk. It is indicated for travelers to endemic areas, people in or moving to endemic regions, and certain laboratory or close-contact exposures. Because it is a plain (unconjugated) polysaccharide, it is not effective in children under 2 years; newer Vi-conjugate vaccines extend protection to infants. This is a vaccine entry based on package-insert/reference information.

moa: The vaccine contains the purified Vi capsular polysaccharide antigen of Salmonella Typhi. After intramuscular injection it elicits a humoral immune response, stimulating B cells to produce anti-Vi IgG antibodies. These antibodies bind the Vi capsule that normally helps the organism evade complement and phagocytosis, promoting opsonization and bacterial clearance and thereby reducing the risk of clinical typhoid fever on subsequent exposure. As a plain (unconjugated) polysaccharide it generates a T-cell-independent response, which is poor in young children and does not produce strong immunologic memory, so protection wanes and boosters are required.

monitor: Immediate hypersensitivity for ~15-30 minutes after injection

preg: The vaccine is inactivated and is not expected to harm the fetus. Use during pregnancy only when clearly needed (e.g., unavoidable travel to a high-risk area), weighing the risk of typhoid against the limited pregnancy data.
lact: Inactivated vaccines, including the Vi polysaccharide typhoid vaccine, are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; the benefit of protecting the mother usually outweighs any theoretical risk.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

interactions.diagnostics: No clinically important effect on laboratory tests.

pearls: Vaccine entry: single-dose, intramuscular, plain (unconjugated) Vi polysaccharide typhoid vaccine
Provides roughly 55-70% protection for about 2-3 years; not effective under 2 years of age
Distinct from the oral live attenuated Ty21a vaccine and from newer Vi-conjugate vaccines (which protect infants and last longer)
Give at least 2 weeks before travel; reinforce food/water precautions as protection is incomplete
Boost every 2-3 years for continued exposure
missed: If a scheduled booster is missed in a person with continued exposure, give it as soon as possible; a single dose still provides protection. There is no need to restart a series, as this is a single-dose vaccine.
overdose: Overdose is not a meaningful concern for a single-dose vaccine. Inadvertent administration of more than the recommended dose is managed with observation and supportive care for any local or systemic reactions.
